summary: The note presents six case studies of social enterprises launched between September 2023 and February 2024, spanning handicrafts, agriculture, solar energy, literacy, healthcare tech and microfinance. Each pairs a founder's vision with measurable social outcomes such as artisan livelihoods, reduced food waste, solar installations, mobile libraries, patient matching and microloans. It concludes that business success need not come at the expense of social value.
one_line: Six case studies of social enterprises founded from late 2023 to early 2024 show how purpose-driven ventures deliver both profit and social impact.
key_facts: Julia Carter founded Rustic Weaves in Arcadia on October 5, 2023, a handicraft social enterprise connecting global markets with local artisans.
Rustic Weaves reinvests 70% of profits back into artisan communities and by April 2024 had partnered with over 500 artisans across 5 countries.
Former investment banker Noah Lee founded Green Harvest Co-op on December 8, 2023, helping small-scale farmers sell directly to consumers and bypass exploitative middlemen.
Green Harvest Co-op used technology to streamline crop selection and distribution, reducing food waste by March 2024, and offered training in organic farming.
Sanjeev Agarwal and Maria Gonzalez launched Luminosity on January 15, 2024, from a small workshop in Austin, Texas, offering renewable energy solutions for low-income households.
By June 2024 Luminosity had outfitted over 2,000 homes with affordable solar systems and created a network of 'solar champions' trained to install and maintain them locally.
Chinedu Okorie founded BookBright in Lagos on September 25, 2023, to fight illiteracy among underprivileged children through mobile libraries.
By February 2024 BookBright had dispatched fleets of mobile libraries, working with local schools and organizations and gaining support from global literacy advocates.

Dr. Amelia Thompson and developer Eric Schultz launched MediMatch in a Boston office on November 12, 2023, to connect patients from marginalized communities with affordable care and subsidized medications.
MediMatch uses AI to match healthcare providers with patients and added mental health counseling by May 2024.
Rachel Kim and Joshua Beckett launched SeedFund on February 10, 2024, providing microloans with minimal barriers to entry and business mentoring to SMEs overlooked by conventional banks.
SeedFund has held workshops since its inception to equip entrepreneurs with business acumen.
